title: Request: Workaround for enterprise Outlook requiring admin approval
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. ### App Thunderbird for Android ### App version 24.0 ### Where did you get the app from? F-Droid ### Android version GrapheneOS ### Device model Google Pixel 8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Attempt to log in to my University of Pittsburgh email account (Microsoft Outlook, OAuth2). 2. Get stuck at a page telling me to contact admins to approve the app. 3. Ask admins to approve Thunderbird for Android and get ghosted/rejected because I'm not important enough :( ### Expected behavior Since Thunderbird for Android and Thunderbird for Desktop are created by the same organizations, if admins approve one, the other should work too. A similar issue was reported here (https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/9048) and was marked as WONTFIX. However, this makes continuity across products (Desktop vs Android) fail. The original suggestion was: > Thunderbird Android should claim to be the same app as Thunderbird Desktop when signing in with a Microsoft account, so that users can continue to use their accounts on mobile and desktop There was an argument presented against it (avoiding putting all eggs in one basket) but I think having access to my email on mobile is more important. Could this be implemented but hidden behind an experimental/advanced setting perhaps? I imagine it's a relatively simple spoof to implement but I could be wrong. ### Actual behavior Though Thunderbird for Desktop is approved and works, Thunderbird for Android doesn't. ### Logs _No response_
